tiles.name: RISC-V CPU B
tiles.purpose: A processor that is never allowed to use the shared memory. It shows that an untrusted tile is stopped inside its own tile.
does: Runs the same demo firmware as CPU A.
Its memory requests are refused by its own bridge, so nothing reaches the network.
Prints “T0 REFUSED” on the UART and lights the RGB LED.

tiles.role: Network interface only; no application in this build
tiles.name: Network tile
tiles.purpose: A router and network interface with nothing attached. It still forwards packets that pass through it, such as memory replies on their way back to tile 3.
does: Forwards packets across the top row of the mesh.
Has no processor or memory of its own in this build.

tiles.role: Shared memory behind the memory front end
tiles.name: Shared memory
tiles.purpose: Memory that the processors share over the network. Its front end checks, on every access, that the sender is allowed in.
does: Receives write and read requests from the network.
Checks the sender’s permission at the moment of each access.
Sends read data back to the requesting tile.

tiles.role: RISC-V CPU tile A with the PQ-Attest endpoint (the attested tile)
tiles.name: RISC-V CPU A
tiles.purpose: The processor that must prove it can be trusted before it may use the shared memory.
does: Measures its own firmware (the first 64 bytes of its instruction memory) with SHA3-256.
Answers the root of trust’s challenge with that measurement and a KMAC128 tag.
Once granted, writes 0xC0DE5A5A to the shared memory, reads it back and prints “T3 PASS”.

tiles.name: Root of trust
tiles.purpose: The security controller. It challenges tile 3, checks the answer and decides whether tile 3 may use the shared memory.
does: Sends CHALLENGE, GRANT and REVOKE to tile 3.
Checks the measurement and tag that tile 3 returns.
Starts after reset and again on button 1; button 2 revokes.

tiles.role: Untrusted SPOOF injection port behind an ingress quarantine
tiles.name: Untrusted port
tiles.purpose: A port used in simulation to inject forged packets. Its quarantine rejects them before they reach the network.
does: Holds incoming packets in a quarantine and rejects forged ones.
Tied off in the board image, so it is only exercised in simulation.

Ball functions are not drawn.

components.name: RISC-V CPU tile B
components.summary: A PicoRV32 processor that is never authorized. When its program asks for the shared memory, its own bridge refuses on the spot and nothing is sent into the network.
detail: Runs the same demo firmware as CPU A (RV32I assembly).
Prints "T0 REFUSED" on the UART and sets LED pattern 0010.
The refused CPU receives a poison value in place of data.

components.name: PicoRV32 core and peripherals
components.summary: The processor with its adapter, address decoder, status registers, UART and GPIO.

components.name: Local memories
components.summary: Instruction and data memory in block RAM. The firmware image is loaded into the instruction memory.

components.name: Measurement window reader
components.summary: Present in every CPU tile. On tile 0 its output is not used for attestation.

components.name: TMEM to NoC bridge
components.summary: Turns a processor memory access into a network request. It never raises a request while the tile is not authorized, so tile 0's requests stop here.

components.name: Tile 1 (no application)

metrics.note: No application logic; only the network interface is built

components.summary: This tile has a router and a network interface but no application. It still forwards packets that pass through router R1.

components.name: Memory front end

metrics.note: Not separately measured: its logic is merged into the network subsystem in the report

components.summary: Stands in front of the shared memory and checks, at the moment of each read or write, that the requesting tile is authorized.

components.name: Shared memory
components.geometryRule: Fixed size; not to scale (block RAM, no LUTs)
components.summary: Block RAM that the tiles share over the network. In the demo, tile 3 writes 0xC0DE5A5A here and reads it back.

components.name: RISC-V CPU tile A
components.summary: A PicoRV32 processor and the one tile that gets attested. Once the root of trust grants access, its program can use the shared memory on tile 2.
detail: Runs the demo firmware (RV32I assembly).
Prints "T3 PASS" on the UART and sets LED pattern 0001 after a correct write and read-back.
Shares the tile's network port with the PQ-Attest endpoint.

components.name: TMEM to NoC bridge
components.summary: Turns a processor memory access into a network request and waits for the response. After a revoke it refuses new requests locally.

components.name: Measurement window reader
components.summary: Reads the first 64 bytes of the instruction memory and hands them to the PQ-Attest endpoint, which hashes them as part of the measurement.

components.name: Local memories
components.summary: Instruction and data memory in block RAM. The firmware image is loaded into the instruction memory.

components.name: PicoRV32 core and peripherals
components.summary: The processor with its adapter, address decoder, status registers, UART and GPIO.

components.name: PQ-Attest endpoint
components.summary: Answers the root of trust for tile 3. It measures the tile with SHA3-256 and returns the measurement with a KMAC128 tag.
detail: Measurement input: tile ID, configuration and a 64-byte window of the instruction memory.
Challenge 224 bits; response payload 512 bits (measurement and tag).
Symmetric cryptography only. No signature scheme is implemented.

components.name: L2 authenticated link
components.summary: Authenticates control packets between tiles 3 and 4 only, so a forged or replayed control packet is rejected.
detail: Each control packet carries a KMAC128 128-bit tag, an 80-bit epoch and a 64-bit sequence number.
One KMAC engine is shared through an arbiter.
Data packets (memory requests and responses) are not tagged.

components.name: RoT verifier
components.summary: The root of trust. It sends a challenge to tile 3, checks the returned measurement and tag, and then grants or revokes access.
detail: Issues CHALLENGE, GRANT and REVOKE.
Attestation starts once after reset and again when button 1 is pressed; button 2 revokes.
There is no periodic re-attestation timer in this build.

components.name: Ingress quarantine
components.summary: Holds anything arriving from the untrusted port and rejects rogue packets before they can enter the network.

components.name: SPOOF port

metrics.note: A port, not a block. Tied off in the board image.

components.summary: An untrusted injection port used in simulation to send forged or replayed packets. In the board image it is tied off, so this attack is not part of the board demo.

components.name: MMCM clock generator
components.clockDomain: input sys_clk_pin (100 MHz), output clk50_mmcm (50 MHz)
components.resetDomain: none (its lock signal starts the design reset)

metrics.note: A device primitive, not LUT logic

components.summary: Turns the board's 100 MHz clock into the single 50 MHz clock that the whole design uses.
